notes: Direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi, chrome impersonation) worked for the homepage, robots.txt and the 3 sitemap files (sitemap-category.xml etc.) but every /c/ category PLP returned a DataDome CAPTCHA (403/interstitial) even reusing session cookies. Headless Playwright hit the same DataDome challenge on both the homepage and category pages. Used the Claude-in-Chrome connector (tier 3) to reach the real rendered site; robots.txt lists ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/Anthropic-ai only under the same generic Disallow rules as User-agent:* (cart/login/search/account paths) - no Claude-specific 'Disallow: /', so no policy_opt_out. Discovery: fetched sitemap-category.xml (298 URLs) and grepped for kerst*/halloween/pasen/valentijn/etc - only Christmas ('kerst') slugs matched. Walked the site's own breadcrumb + sibling filter-chip tabs from the root 'Onze kerstcollectie' (hash nb49f74884a8d9b0c042cb19ecea80fbf7ad78a9, same node id as the French site's 'Toute la collection Noel' in se96.json) down through every branch, reading each chip's real href via the DOM (not guessing from the sitemap's Dutch slugs, which turned out stale in places). This produced a complete, verified Christmas tree. Excluded as currently unavailable (site itself returns 'Deze pagina is niet meer beschikbaar' for these exact hrefs, confirmed on repeat/fresh navigation, i.e. genuinely 0-stock/out-of-season right now, not a bad URL): Adventskalender (Advent Calendar), Kerstbomen (Christmas Trees), Kerstboomversiering (Christmas Tree Decorations) and its own likely children Kerstballen (Christmas Baubles) and Kersthangers (Christmas Hanging Ornaments), Kerstkransen (Christmas Wreaths), and kerst-lichtjes-slingers-en-pieken (a stale sitemap URL, hash n7ac596952a6204a6a19f528f1e8b2fbdbba1921, not linked from any current chip). Also checked the French site's additional hash node for 'Outdoor Christmas Decorations' (nb05b60b079f5fe38f494dcab3d5e9ba121da940): on BE/nl this hash silently falls back to the parent 'Kerstversiering' listing rather than erroring, i.e. it is not a distinct category on this storefront - excluded. Two leaf categories (Gift Wrap and Packaging / Gift Bags) have generic, non-'kerst' names but their only breadcrumb path is Home > Onze kerstcollectie > <name>, i.e. the site's own taxonomy files them exclusively under the Christmas collection - kept per the coexistence rule and flagged for a second look, matching how se96.json (FR) treated the identical two hash nodes. Qty = each page's own 'N artikelen' count, read directly off the rendered PLP (zoomed screenshot to confirm the digits). Parent/child totals are not additive on this site (e.g. Kerstservies=81 vs its 3 children summing to 62; Kersttafeldecoratie=102 vs children summing to 94) so parent nodes with real children are kept as grouping rows (qty null) rather than double-counted, exactly as se96.json did for this same site. Searched the live internal search (found via the real search box, URL pattern /BE/nl/q/<term>, confirmed discriminating against a nonsense query = '0 resultaat') for halloween (0 results) and pinksteren/Pentecost (0 results) - no Halloween or other-festival category exists. 'pasen' (Easter, 2 hits) and 'valentijn' (Valentine, 22 hits) return only individual products, not a dedicated category node - no Easter/Valentine PLP exists in the nav or sitemap, so no rows created (search hits are discovery-only, never proof, per rules). The Category facet on a 'kerst' search (61 hits) surfaced only the Christmas nodes already captured, plus a handful of generic non-seasonal categories (Food storage boxes, Cups and mugs, Cushions and covers, Paper napkins, Flat plates, Salad bowls and dishes, Wine and cocktail accessories) each with 1-2 incidentally Christmas-patterned products filed under an ordinary product category, not a seasonal one - excluded per Rule 5/6 (seasonal product type != seasonal category). No Diwali/Eid/other-festival taxonomy found anywhere in nav, sitemap or search. Closed the browser tab at the end of the run.
